text:
Maria L: Heads-up — noticed a spike in TTFT 99p for /v1/chat on prod-nyc between 09:20–09:35 UTC. Prequeue and scheduling look normal, but decode kernel time jumps ~2.1x on a subset of requests.
Rajesh: Hmm. Any route-specific tagging? Could be kv cache miss pattern or a kernel selector flip.
Maria L: Right. I sliced by model+route and saw it only for gpt-small-ish routes (quantized) serving bursty short prompts. Percentiles: TTFT p50=18ms p95=70ms p99=210ms. Decode kernel contribution goes from ~30% -> ~65% on the bad tail.
Toshi: Do we have token-level attribution metrics enabled for those requests? Might need per-token kernel_time + io_wait labels.
Maria L: Currently we emit token_timing with labels {kernel, kv_hit, batch_size} but the kernel label isn't broken out by selector reason (e.g., fallback_kernel vs fused_kernel_vs_generic). Proposing to add kernel_choice and cache_prefetch labels.
Elaine: Good idea. Without kernel_choice we can't tell if kernel selection changed due to sequence_len or quantization compatibility. Also we should check batcher behavior — are those requests getting microbatched with larger-than-expected batches?
Maria L: I pulled a raw sample from td: 200 records. Example rows: 
```
request_id=abc123 model=gpt-q1 route=/v1/chat tokens=18 batch_size=6 kernel_time_ms=156 kv_hit=false kernel_impl=fallback
```
Rajesh: That suggests a fallback path (fallback kernel) being used when batch_size>1 and seq_len small. Kernel might be taking slower path if vectorized instructions not chosen.
Toshi: Can you share the prom query you used? I can try correlate with kvcache miss rate.
Maria L: Prom query I ran: 
```
sum by(kernel_impl,route)(rate(runtime_token_kernel_time_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum by(kernel_impl,route)(rate(runtime_token_kernel_time_seconds_count[5m]))
```
Gave average kernel latency by kernel_impl. But we need high percentiles, so I used clickhouse: 
```
SELECT kernel_impl, quantiles(0.5,0.95,0.99)(kernel_time_ms) FROM token_timings WHERE route='/v1/chat' AND ts>now()-3600 GROUP BY kernel_impl
```
Elaine: Nice. Two practical things: 1) increase token-level sampling for that route to 100% for 30m window to capture more KV/cache context; 2) emit kernel_choice enum (fused|fallback|generic|cuda-mmac) in the event stream.
infra-bot: @Maria L — sampling rate updated for /v1/chat on cluster prod-nyc to 100% for 30m.
Maria L: thx infra-bot :raised_hands: — also scheduled a short-lived dashboard update: new panel showing per-route TTFT p99 with stacked bars for kernel_impl fractions and kv_hit rate.
Rajesh: For dashboard metric names, use runtime.token.kernel_time_ms:percentile and runtime.token.kv_hit:ratio with labels route, model, kernel_impl. That'll make cross-correlation easier.
Toshi: Also recommend instrumenting kernel selector to emit selection_reason tags (seq_len_bucket, quant_compat, batcher_policy) — that's cheap and will help root cause quickly.
Maria L: Agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to add kernel_choice and selection_reason to the telemetry envelope (runtime side), and a separate PR to the observability team for the dashboard panels.
Elaine: Can you add an action item to verify whether older kernel merges (last release) introduced selector heuristics change? We had a selector tweak in build 2026.5.
Maria L: noted — will diff builds and correlate. Action items: 1) Maria — PR for kernel_choice + selection_reason (due EOD). 2) Rajesh/Toshi — run cross-correlation job between token_kernel_time p99 and kv_miss rate over last 24h (due tomorrow AM). 3) Elaine — dashboard PR for per-route stacked kernel breakdown (due EOD).
Rajesh: I'll also run a quick microbench replicating small-batch short-prompt workload locally to reproduce.
Toshi: If we reproduce, we should try toggling selector heuristics and report s/s improvements.
Maria L: Thanks all — we'll reconvene after the sampling window. If anyone sees more anomalies ping here. :eyes:
